links.comparator_used: Web-search grounding (open web search); MedRAG over its own databases was also tested
links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of genetic variant summaries (5-point Likert scale), and clinically significant hallucinations
links.effect: Accuracy 4.76 (+0.74) and completeness 4.94 (+0.84) versus web-search grounding; fewer hallucinations such as incorrect pathogenicity classification and summarizing the wrong variant
links.tradeoff: Limited coverage in the corpus hurts: MedRAG failed to generate clinically useful summaries because its databases held limited relevant information, and it did worse than web search.
links.quote: Precision Grounding outperformed web-search grounding, achieving significantly higher accuracy and completeness scores, which were based on a 5-point Likert-Scale of 4.76 (+0.74) and 4.94 (+0.84), respectively.
